data.name: अनिल
data.gender_notes: अनिल is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Anil is the Sanskrit name for air and wind. In Hindu mythology, Anil is the god of wind and is considered to be the younger brother of Agni, the god of fire. The name अनिल carries the meaning “Air, Wind” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose अनिल usually hope their child will grow to embody air, wind and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the power of change and transformation, as wind brings change to the environment.
data.etymology: अनिल belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Air, Wind.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of अनिल total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: Anil holds significant cultural importance in Hinduism, where he is one of the eight major Vayus or winds, and is a prominent figure in Vedic literature. He is commonly invoked in rituals to bring changes, often symbolizing new beginnings or fresh starts. The legend of Lord Rama's return to Ayodhya, after defeating Ravana, is marked by the arrival of Anil, which brought fresh air and heralded a new era.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Anil represents the principle of change and transformation. He signifies the unconscious forces of nature that blow through our lives, shaping and shaping our experiences. In fact, the name Anil can be considered a reminder of the ever-present breath of life - Prana - that keeps us connected to the world around us. Through his personification as a god, Anil inspires us to be open and adaptable, embracing the winds of change, even when they seem challenging.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Anil means "wind" or "breath of life" in Sanskrit. It symbolizes the dynamic and ever-changing nature of life, representing the element of air and the power of movement.
